clue.text: Play about cider-maker's commission

indicators.note: about tells us the word for play goes round the other letters

parts.note: to play a part is to act

indicators.note: a maker turns raw material into something new, so the letters of cider are remade

explanation.surface: A drama concerning a cider producer's fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maker's' rearranges CIDER into CREDI, and 'about' puts ACT around it: AC + CREDI + T.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission someone is to authorise or appoint them officially, which is what accrediting does.

clue.text: Charge a couple of hundred to operate

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundreds are CC
to operate a machine is to use it

explanation.surface: Being billed two hundred to run something.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a crime is to formally blame them for it.

clue.text: Cheat and blackguard come to an agreement

parts.note: to con someone is to swindle them
a cur is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: A swindler and a scoundrel strike a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share an opinion, to be of one mind with someone.

clue.text: Protection for the pupil

parts.note: reads like a guardian for a schoolchild, but the pupil is the dark centre of the eye, shielded by a fold of skin

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin over the eye closes to shield the pupil from dust and light.

clue.text: Cheek outside right — such temerity!

indicators.note: outside says the word for cheek sits around the letter for right

parts.note: cheek, as in insolence, is impudence

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at someone's audacity in cheeking a person on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts IMPUDENCE around R, which goes in after IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, a lack of caution and good sense.

clue.text: An officer of the law makes little money

definitions.meaning: low-value coins such as pennies, made of or named after the reddish metal

explanation.surface: Policemen are poorly paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: slang for a policeman, and small brown coins of low value.

clue.text: Yielding nothing to pass on in disposition

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in says the word for passing on goes inside the word for disposition

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or disposition
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: Giving nothing away to an heir, by temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DIE inside BENT after its E, giving BEDIENT, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone yielding readily submits to others, doing as they are told.

clue.text: Carries on doggedly and quietly resists change

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of resists

explanation.surface: A stubborn person keeps going and silently opposes reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges RESISTS into ERSISTS, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere stubbornly in spite of difficulty or opposition.

clue.text: Diffident about losing interest

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
someone tiring of something is losing interest in it

explanation.surface: A shy person who gets bored.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffident people are shy and reserved, keeping out of the limelight.

clue.text: Many continually sweet-talk, finding only disdain

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
on, as in going on and on, means continually
to sweet-talk someone is to coax or tempt them

explanation.surface: Lots of people keep flattering, but meet only scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is scorn, the feeling that someone is beneath consideration.

clue.text: Some lifer retaken into custody — a real beast!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recaptured life prisoner is jailed again, a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'into custody', which is surface only; the definition is 'a real beast', since the answer is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A polecat-like animal used for hunting rabbits, so a genuine creature.

clue.text: Hard-working bosses without financial commitment

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the word for bosses goes around the other letters

parts.note: bosses are ornamental studs
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Diligent managers who owe nobody money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: STUDS goes around IOU, giving STUD-IOU-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person applies themselves diligently to study.

clue.text: Being more orderly, Diana will get involved in the row

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Di is a short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: Diana joins a quarrel and calms it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface, but here it rhymes with 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater, in better order, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: There's a total lack of choice still

definitions.text: There's a total lack of choice
definitions.meaning: everything is identical, so there is nothing to choose between

explanation.surface: No options at all, even now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'identical in every case' and 'nevertheless', used as a sentence adverb.

clue.text: A capital military leader!

definitions.meaning: the capital city of New Zealand
the duke who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo

explanation.surface: An excellent general!
explanation.definitionFit: Both the New Zealand capital and the victor of Waterloo, the Iron Duke, bear the name.

clue.text: An artist's main work

parts.note: reads as a painter's masterpiece, but main is the old word for the ocean, so this is a painting of the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: A picture showing a view of the ocean, the main in poetic language.

clue.text: Plaster around a south window

indicators.note: around says the word for plaster is placed round the other letters

parts.note: plaster and cement are both building mortars
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Rendering round a south-facing window.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged window that opens outward like a door.

clue.text: A horse-not as ill as it might appear

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the letters of the words before it could appear in another order

explanation.surface: A horse in better health than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it might appear' rearranges NOTASILL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male of the equine species.

clue.text: Allowance for expansion

parts.note: sounds like a budget for growth, but means the physical property of stretching and springing back

explanation.definitionFit: The property of a material that lets it stretch and then return to shape.

clue.text: Dancing girl taking part accepting a pound

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for part holds the other letters

parts.note: some means a part of a whole
L stands for libra, the pound

explanation.surface: A dancer joining in and taking a pound as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts A and L inside SOME: S-AL-OME.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical princess who danced the dance of the seven veils for Herod.

clue.text: Set around a royal residence

indicators.note: around says the word for set goes round the letter A

parts.note: to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Placed near a home of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts PLACE around A, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: The official residence of a monarch, like Buckingham.

clue.text: Centre being done over in modern style

indicators.note: something done over has been redone or roughed up, so the letters of centre are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town centre being refurbished in contemporary design.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent things belong to the present era, much as modern ones do.

clue.text: Grows fat and fit on board

indicators.note: on, as in on board a ship, says the word for fit goes inside the letters for a steamship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the board of on board
fit and healthy means well

explanation.surface: Someone gets plump and healthy on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On board conventionally means inside SS, steamship: WELL inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand, to get bigger, as a fattening body does.

clue.text: An Amerind headed back — sensible, that

indicators.note: back says the word for headed is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to head a group is to lead it, so headed is led
sensible in its sense of conscious means aware

explanation.surface: A Native American who led a retreat, and wisely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LED into DEL. The Delaware, or Lenape, are a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people, the Lenape, also giving its name to a US state.

clue.text: Woman cooking A1 meal

indicators.note: cooking a dish mixes up its ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with a figure 1 that doubles as the letter I

explanation.surface: A woman preparing a first-rate dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges AI (A1, its 1 standing for I) plus MEAL into a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, an example of a woman.

clue.text: Nobility and restraint when mature?

parts.note: a bar is something that restrains or blocks
on, as in on arrival, means at the time of
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Asking whether aristocrats acquire self-control with age.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of barons, the peerage or aristocracy as a class.

clue.text: Range of formerly temporary accommodation

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tent is shelter put up for a short time

explanation.surface: The scope of former camping lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is the scope, size or reach of something.

clue.text: Making a crack about always showing respect

indicators.note: about says the word for making a crack goes around the word for always

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
ever means always, as in ever after

explanation.surface: Constantly cracking jokes while showing deference.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means feeling or showing deep, solemn regard.
